prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mathematics and physics.
Solving differential equations and applications of Fourier and Laplace transforms.
Knowledge of the fundamental elements of electrical engineering.
Knowledge of the fundamentals of automation.

learning_outcomes.text: Introduce students to bioengineering, providing them with the basic knowledge necessary to understand biomedical systems and the fundamentals of biomedical instrumentation.
Understand the main physiological systems, from an anatomical and functional point of view, and the origin of physiological signals, including through the use of models.
Understand the main systems for the collection and presentation of pathophysiological signals and for monitoring and functional assistance.
Understand techniques for processing biomedical data and signals.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Bioengineering
Definition of Bioengineering, situation in Italy and Europe, fields of application, and objectives
Models in physiology and medicine: Central and peripheral nervous system
Neurons and synapses
Membrane potential and action potential generation
Conduction velocity and its measurement
Sensory system: sensory transducers
Muscular system: mechanical model of the muscle, contraction, simple shock, tetanus, and active state
Musculoskeletal and postural system: feedback control, reflex arc, spindles, and Golgi tendon organ
Electrical nerve and muscle stimulation
Cardiac and vascular system: mechanical function of the heart, cardiac electrical activity, elements of hemodynamics
Biomedical instrumentation: Origin and collection of physiological signals
Issues related to signal transduction, preparation, and processing
Bioimaging instrumentation: overview of radiological equipment and optical and electron microscopy
Amplifiers for biomedical use
Electrocardiogram (ECG), electroencephalogram (EEG), electromyogram (EMG), pressure, flow, respiration, temperature
Equipment for monitoring key vital signs
Ultrasound and flow assessment devices
Pacemakers, defibrillators, and cardioverters
Hemodialysis and ventilators
Biomedical Signal and Data Processing: Introduction to biological signals
Morphological and bandwidth characteristics of the main biomedical signals
Issues about biomedical signal and data acquisition, conditioning, sampling, quantization, and storage
Digital signal processing in the time and frequency domains
Methods for analyzing correlated and uncorrelated signals
Analysis of electrocardiographic, pressure, flow, electroencephalographic, evoked potential, and electromyographic signals
Principles of electrical safety
assessment_rules: The assessment is through an oral exam, evaluating knowledge, application ability, critical thinking, and clarity of presentation. The oral exam considers maturity, presentation quality, critical spirit, independence of judgment, and mastery of scientific language. It may include aspects of classroom exercises and laboratory projects. The final grade, expressed in thirtieths, will be based on satisfying these requirements. Honours may be awarded for full satisfaction of assessment criteria.
bibliography: Enderle, J., & Bronzino, J. (Eds.). (2012). Introduction to biomedical engineering. Academic press.
Webster, J. G. (Ed.). (2009). Medical instrumentation: application and design. John Wiley & Sons.
Silbernagl, Stefan, et al. Fisiologia: atlante tascabile. CEA, 2018.
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Elettronica E Biomedica (Electronics And Biomedical Engineering), classe L-8 Classe delle lauree in Ingegneria dell'informazione
